scope: Extant Primatial Cathedral of Bogotá with its current twin belfries, restored pediment, plaza steps, long tiled roofs and mapped secondary wings.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The cathedral records the changes after the 1827 earthquake and the twentieth-century rebuilding of the upper facade and twin towers with stone-clad reinforced concrete.
The collection identifies the 1846 watercolor and Edward Walhouse Mark as artist, with inventory number AP0057.
The collection identifies the artist’s death in 1895.
The archival account reports a total height of 46 metres and an area of about 5,022 square metres.
The city describes the cathedral and nearby Capilla del Sagrario as separate parts of the Plaza de Bolívar ensemble.
